text_post: I think the major contributor to inceldom/loveshy is Impostor syndrome. which is essentially the feeling of being an impostor in various situations and not being capable enough or as good as other people to fulfill a role or a task, and you are afraid of being outed as the fraud you think you are. This also plays out in dating whenever it comes to approaching or flirting with girls the awkwardness and fear is basically a form of impostor syndrome.  Ironic thing is most of us probably know exactly what we should be doing in dating situations, and we could even tell other men what to do in a given situation, but we find it neigh impossible to do in person when on the spot. I think I may have a possible solution for this. It came to me over the weekend when I inexplicably started feeling really good about myself and I just seemed to be doing everything right both in the context of my work and socializing. I just naturally seemed to know what to say to people. I know I can't maintain that positive mindset, what I would call my Ideal Self for more than a day, its happened before and it usually lasts no more than a day because the normal setbacks of day to day life bring me back to my typical unsure self, BUT I think if I actively try to imagine what my "Ideal self"  would do in every circumstance I can at least temporary imitate a more confident version of myself and counteract the Impostor Syndrome that I frequently feel. So far it seems to be showing some progress.  What do you guys think? do you think envisioning your Ideal self can help in being more confident?
